items.title: Why are your ads spending but not selling?
items.excerpt: Four questions that show you where the problem is before you raise the budget.

body.text: The first thing most business owners do when results drop: raise the budget, try a new platform, or change the design. In most cases I've seen, the problem was none of these.
Before you touch the ad, answer these four questions honestly:
1. Is your offer clear in two seconds?

If someone sees your ad while scrolling fast, do they know what you sell, who it's for, and why they should buy from you specifically? If the answer needs explaining, your ad is paying the price for an unclear offer.
2. Are you talking to the right audience?
The same product sells to two audiences in two different ways. A gift is not the same as personal use, and the decision maker is not always the user. Decide who pays, and what matters to them.
3. Does your message match what the customer is looking for?
Customers aren't searching for "high quality at competitive prices". They're looking for a solution to a specific problem. Use their words, not yours.
4. Are your numbers honest?
Wrong tracking means wrong decisions. Make sure your pixel and GA4 record sales correctly before you judge any campaign.

end.text: Fix these four, and every platform becomes cheaper and clearer. That's what I call:

items.title: SEO isn't a luxury: sales without ads
items.excerpt: How Google becomes a steady source of sales for your store, especially in peak seasons.

body.text: For one store I worked with, organic search from Google brought in more than SAR 460K in sales within a year, including the National Day season, the store's most successful ever. All of it without paying a single riyal per click.
Ads stop the moment the budget stops. SEO builds an asset that works for you every day. These are the things that make the difference:
Start with what people search for
Learn the words your customers type into Google, and build your product and category pages around them, not around internal names nobody knows.
Prepare for seasons well in advance
Seasonal pages like National Day, Ramadan and Eid need time to rank on Google. Prepare them weeks before the season, not the same week.
Get the technical basics right
Site speed, clear titles, a description for every page, and logical internal links. Simple things with a big impact.
Track the right numbers
Impressions and clicks matter, but the most important number is sales from organic search in GA4. That's what tells you SEO is really working.

items.title: Running a service business? Measure leads, not clicks
items.excerpt: The number to track when your goal is inquiries, not online sales.

body.text: If your business is a clinic, an office, or any service that isn't sold online directly, most of the numbers in your ads dashboard mean very little. Clicks and impressions look nice, but they don't pay salaries.
The number that matters: cost per lead
How much did you pay for one person to actually contact you? A WhatsApp message, a call, or a completed form. That's the number to compare campaigns with.
Then: how many of them became real customers?
A campaign that brings cheap leads but nobody books is worse than a pricier one that brings serious people. Follow up with your team on what happened with every lead.
Offer before targeting
In services, people buy trust. Make clear what sets you apart, and show proof: results, client reviews, or certifications. And keep the contact step simple and obvious.
Don't judge too fast
The decision cycle for services is longer than for online stores. Give a campaign enough time before you stop it.

about.title: I'm Mariam Wajeh Alawar
about.lead: Digital marketing consultant, master's in computer information systems, and founder of Clickat agency. Since 2014 I've been helping brands and charities across the Gulf sell more and spend less.

story.text: In 2014 I entered marketing through content, as content manager at Toot. Three years of writing, testing and learning what makes people stop, read and buy.

In 2017 I finished a master's in computer information systems and started seeing marketing through data. I freelanced, founded Creativity in 2018, then Clickat, a paid advertising agency, in 2022, and went on to work with international organizations like Qatar Charity and Gaza Sky Geeks.
More than 200 brands taught me that the ad is rarely the problem. Content gives me the message, and data gives me the proof. That's what I call:
